Chengtu,
March 28, 1935
For many months China National Aviation Corporation has
been planning the extension of its Yangtsze River line from Chungking
to Kweiyang and Yunnan-fu.
Recently a tri-motored Ford with new
motors and adjustable pitch propellers arrived in Shanghai and on
Monday March 25th we started out from Shanghai.
"We" means Pilot
co-pilot Thom and a Chinese radio operator,
those three
comprising the crew.
As part of the working organization the As-
sistant Operations Manager K. I. Nieh was a passenger.
very intelligent Chinese whose native home is Kweiyang and who has
already made a flight with Chief Pilot Allison to Yunnan-fu.
nother passenger was Lyons, an American mechanic, who will have
charge of maintaining the plane with his headquarters at Chungking.
Several officials and direotors of CNAC promised to join the party
but all backed out at the last moment except one of the Chinese
directors, Ki Chun who is a good friend of mine.
He went to school
at Amherst when I was in College there. The whole party - seven in
We Left Shanghai Monday morning March
25th at 8 o'clock
and arrived at Hankow at 11:30 a.m.
Then we refueled and
got off
at 12:30 for Chungking.
We followed the Yangtze through the
Gorges (which are more impressive every time I see them) and ar-
rived at Chungking at 4:45 p.m.
It was a grand trip. Monday
night Ki Chun and I spent on the U.S.S. Yangtsze River Patrol boat
"Palos" as the guests of Capt. Settle who made the stratosphere
flight several years ago. Col. Drysdaletpalos".
American Military Intel-
11 gence Officer was also a guest on the
We learned a lot
about political and military manoeuvers in Szechuen Province and
Kwe ichow.
On Tuesday the crew had to work on the Ford making minor
adjustments and servicing the motors.
Wednesday the pilot, co-pilot
and radio operator were to make the
first flight to Kweiyang and
return, and the plan was to have them fly as light as possible so
only Mr. Nieh went along as & passenger.
The weather was bad Wednes-
day and therefore the flight was postponed until Thursday.
In the
meantime Ki Chun and I flew to Chengtu on the regular plane and
now as I write this letter, Friday morning March 29th we are on our
way back to Chungking•
Tuesday morning we crossed the Yangtze from the opposite
bank where the Palos was anchored and spent the day with friends of
One of them, a Mr. Wu, is a graduate of M.I.T. and built
the Chungking light plant.
He showed us around the city and found
quarters for us there is no hotel in Chungking.
We left our bags
at the Bank of Chungking where adjoining the directors room they
have two rooms for visiting friends.
Ki Chun's friend told us in
recommending these quarters that we would have the only flush toilet
The President of the Bank did everything possible
make us comfortable.
We called on General Yu, the Vice-Minister of
Communications Tuesday morning and had a long
talk with him.
just recently returned from a trip around the world and is now on
an inspection trip around China.
He flew up to Chengtu on a special
flight Tuesday afternoon. After our call on General Yu we took a
drive around town - there are only three streets where autos can
run - all the rest is by sedan chair.
Then we had Chinese lunch and
in the afternoon we drove out to inspect the road which leads to
Chengtu.
I don't wonder that it is not used much.
Very rough
and where we climbed up over a mountain range there were evidences
all along of land slides - big rocks everywhere on the road, some
of which our chauffeur had to remove - others he just dodged.

Therefore the well trained disciplined troops of Chiang Kai-shek
which pay for what they take and live in barracks instead of
moving into the homes of the populace have been welcomed and
Szechuen Province should prosper greatly from now on.

We returned to Chungking on Friday March 29th and started
for Kweiyang on
Saturday but had to turn back on account of clouds
closing the mountain
tops and passes.
We will try again on
Sunday and I'll tell you about
that part of the trip in another
letter - this one is

As ever
